draft.title: Mammals, primates and hominins
card: Mammals
Mammals have hair or fur, mammary glands that make milk, and three middle ear bones. They are warm-blooded.
Primates
Primates are mammals with grasping hands and feet, nails instead of claws, and forward-facing eyes that give good depth perception. Most also have large brains for their body size.
Hominoids
Hominoids are primates with no tail and a broad chest. They include gibbons, orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees and humans.
Hominins
Hominins are hominoids on the human line after it split from the chimpanzee line. They walked upright on two legs, and modern humans are the only living hominin.
draft.remember: Each group sits inside the one before it, so humans are mammals, primates, hominoids and hominins.

a.q: Which feature do humans share with all primates but NOT with all mammals?
opts: Three bones in the middle ear
Hair covering at least part of the body
a.why: Forward-facing eyes are a primate feature. Milk, middle ear bones and hair are shared by all mammals, so they do not separate primates from other mammals.
a.clue: Look for the feature that the mammal line does not list.

b.q: A scientist studies a tailless animal that climbs trees and walks on all fours, with a broad chest. It is not on the human line. Which group does it certainly belong to?
b.why: No tail and a broad chest place it in the hominoids, like a gorilla. It is not on the human line and does not walk upright, so it is not a hominin. Being a hominoid also makes it a primate and a mammal, so the last two options are wrong.
b.clue: Check the tail and chest first, then ask if it is on the human line.

problems.detail: The question never says the animal is a primate, yet asks which group it 'certainly' belongs to. Being tailless with a broad chest does not by itself make an animal a hominoid, since some other mammals and even some monkeys lack tails. Stating that it is a primate (or an ape) would make the answer certain.

The why says 'the last two options are wrong', which depends on option order. In the order shown, the last option is the intended answer. The why also never explains why 'Hominins, but not hominoids' is wrong (every hominin is a hominoid).

check.summary: The card and question a are sound. Question b says 'certainly' without stating the animal is a primate, and its why refers to 'the last two options', which breaks when options are shuffled and here points at the correct answer.
